title: A Lean formalization of the finite-support empirical DRO reduction
claim: For a sample of positive finite size classified among finitely many support points, the sample-weight Burg uncertainty set and the support-weight Burg ball attain exactly the same objective values. Therefore their lower and upper robust values agree at the exact stated radius scaling.
supporting_scope: Aggregation preserves the objective and can only decrease Burg divergence, by logarithm concavity within each nonempty class.
Equal splitting of each support mass over its observations preserves both the objective and Burg divergence.
Empty classes have zero mass; observed classes have strictly positive mass. The extended-real generator excludes zero observation weights at finite radius.

formal_targets.contribution_scope: Complete aggregation of feasible sample weights into finite-support Burg-ball weights, with exact objective preservation and empty-class handling for every positive sample size and real radius.

Complete splitting of support weights equally among observed sample classes, with exact divergence and objective preservation; handles unobserved support points using the explicit absolute-continuity condition.

Complete finite-support empirical DRO reduction: equality of lower and upper robust values, established via equality of attainable objective sets with exact radius scaling. No asymptotic statistical coverage claim.
